PRINCIPLE: Memory system exists to carry personal context across sessions, not to index codebases
FACT: Most frustrating thing is re-introducing himself every session — 'I code fast', 'I'm doing YouTube', 'I hate markdown files'
CONTEXT: These facts should live globally and surface everywhere regardless of project — working on iOS, web, scripts, video — same person
WHAT HE WANTS: Submit a prompt, keywords trigger associative retrieval, one-sentence context injections, model can pull thread for more
WHAT HE DOES NOT WANT: Code knowledge graph, cross-project architectural awareness, documentation indexing
EXAMPLE: Asking about Whisnap → surfaces 'backend already implemented, just needs correct API call' not general technical docs
KEY QUOTE: 'It's more that it understands me. That's the thing I need the most.'
APPLICATION: Prioritize personal/philosophical global memories heavily. Technical project memories are secondary. Never capture technical minutiae.
